text:
The Devils went out and got Connor Hellebuyck for nights exactly like this one. Mike Fink of The Hockey News said as much midway through it: the offense wasn't there, the team looked tired, and New Jersey wasn't in the game without its goalie. Hellebuyck made 22 saves on 24 shots, saved 1.29 goals more than the chances deserved, and then stopped all three Columbus shooters in the shootout. The Devils won 3-2 and swept the home-and-home, two days after a 3-2 regulation win over the same team.

Columbus had the better of it most of the night. The Blue Jackets out-chanced New Jersey 3.29 to 2.83 in expected goals (our measure of chance quality), and by our replays of every shot they deserved to win 58% of the time. Nico Hischier opened the scoring at 8:06 of the first off Jesper Bratt. Cole Sillinger tied it in the second after a turnover in the Devils' zone, Evan Rodrigues restored the lead on a power play 37 seconds before the second intermission, and Luca Del Bel Belluz, a 2022 second-round pick, tied it again with a slap shot at 8:48 of the third. That goal lifted Columbus's win chance from 21% to 52%, the biggest swing of the night. Matthew Knies, the former Maple Leaf who has found a new home in Columbus, had the best look that didn't go in, a 26% chance stopped by Hellebuyck.

Cam Talbot was every bit as good at the other end and added more wins than anyone in the building by our measure. His biggest moment was a stop on Jack Hughes in overtime, the single most valuable save of the game. Kent Johnson played 24:12, a huge number for a forward, and was on the ice for 1.44 expected goals for and 0.47 against.

In the shootout, Arseny Gritsyuk scored in the first round and that was enough. Charlie Coyle, Valeri Nichushkin and Johnson were all stopped. New Jersey heads into Thanksgiving with the second-best record in the Metropolitan, per Fink, even if neither win this week was the Devils at their best. Columbus gets a point and the sense that it deserved more.
headline: Hellebuyck carries tired Devils to a shootout sweep
